idea-plugin.name: Newspeak (ns-next)
idea-plugin.description:
Support for Newspeak .ns modules, from the ns-next runtime.

  • Syntax highlighting as you type, with brace matching, block comments, TODO markers and spell checking in comments and strings.
  • Errors as you type: every lexer, parser and resolver error ns-next reports before running a module, with ns-next's own message.
  • Semantic colouring from ns-next's resolver: parameters, locals, slots, nested classes and sends.
  • Code folding from ns-next's parser: comments, class bodies and class sides, method bodies, closures and slot sections — kept while a file has syntax errors.
  • A structure view and breadcrumbs from ns-next's parser: each class with its factory, its slots and methods with their access shown as in Java, its class-side methods marked static as in Java, and sticky lines — kept while a file has syntax errors.
  • Completion and validation in newspeak.json, ns-next's project file, from its schema.
  • Running and benchmarking a project from its newspeak.json: a play button beside main and beside each script opens Run and Benchmark, which create a "Newspeak" run configuration starting ns-next run or ns-next bench.

The language server, ns-next-analyzer, is bundled for the platform the plugin was built on. Where none is bundled, the plugin says so; build it with cargo build -p ns-analyzer --release and set its path under Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Newspeak.

The runtime, ns-next, is not bundled. Build it with cargo build -p ns-cli --release and set the ns-next path in the same settings; a Newspeak run configuration refuses to start without it.
